papers.title: Plasma eMTBR-tau as a marker of clinical stage and progression across the Alzheimer's disease continuum
papers.abstract: Importance: Plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration may help characterise progression across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. Plasma eMTBR-tau243 has been associated with tau pathology and cognitive decline. Whether plasma eMTBR-tau levels differ across subjective cognitive decline (SCD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD dementia, between MCI subtypes, or best discriminate subsequent clinical progression in brain health and memory clinic populations remains unclear. Objective: To compare plasma eMTBR-tau and selected biomarkers of neurodegeneration, neuropathology, and neuroinflammation across the AD continuum by pTau217 and APOE {epsilon}4 status, and explore their associations with clinical progression over two years. Design: Observational cohort study with longitudinal follow-up in a subset of participants. Setting: Healthy Brain Ageing (HBA) brain health and memory clinic, Sydney, Australia. Participants underwent assessment between October 2018 and April 2026. Participants: Cross-sectional analysis included 436 participants; 166 were followed up approximately two years later. Exposures: Plasma biomarker quantification using the NULISAseq Neuro 220 Panel, clinical classification by multidisciplinary memory clinic assessment, plasma pTau217 status (SIMOA ALZpath), and APOE {epsilon}4 carrier status. Main Outcomes and Measures: Fasting blood was collected on the morning of assessment. Plasma was analysed using the NULISAseq Neuro 220 panel. Relative biomarker abundance was compared across clinical and biomarker-defined groups. BD-pTau217 and eMTBR-tau levels at the preceding assessment were modelled individually and jointly to assess SCD-to-MCI progression and MCI-to-AD conversion over approximately two years of follow-up. Results: Among 436 participants (mean [SD] age, 70.2 [8.0] years; 67.2% female), 186 had SCD, 228 MCI, and 22 AD dementia. Among 221 biomarkers, phosphorylated tau analytes (pTau181/T205/T212/217/231) dominated clinical group differences, while eMTBR-tau showed the largest adjusted differences: 1.69-fold higher in MCI than SCD, 6.55-fold higher in AD than SCD and 3.88-fold higher in AD than MCI (all FDR-adjusted P < .001). eMTBR-tau was higher in multidomain amnestic MCI than in SCD, and in pTau217-positive than in pTau217-negative individuals. In the exploratory MCI-to-AD analysis (6/40 converted over 2 years), eMTBR-tau at the preceding assessment showed higher cross-validated discrimination of MCI-to-AD conversion than BD-pTau217 (AUC, 0.936 vs. 0.882). Conclusions and Relevance: Clinical stages across the AD continuum are defined by a tau-dominant pattern. eMTBR-tau showed prominent stage-related differences, supporting its further evaluation as a marker of clinical progression.

papers.title: Age and sex impact resting-state EEG aperiodic activity beyond symptom associations in persistent post-concussive symptoms
papers.abstract: Objective: to investigate whether resting-state EEG aperiodic parameters (i.e., offset and exponent) are associated with symptom burden and demographic factors in patients with persistent post-concussive symptoms (PPCS) and differ from healthy controls. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, resting-state eye-closed high-density EEG was recorded in patients with PPCS and in age-matched healthy controls. Aperiodic parameters were extracted from EEG power spectra. In patients, hierarchical multiple linear regression models included age and sex as a base model, with additional demographic and clinical symptoms entered separately. Patient-control differences were assessed using multiple linear regression adjusted for age and sex. Results: Seventy patients with PPCS (54 female; 39.57 {+/-}12.21 y.; 109.5 [76.5; 196] days post-concussion) recruited from a concussion care pathway and 38 healthy controls (17 female; 39.61{+/-} 13.57 y.) were included. In patients, younger age and male sex were associated with higher offset and exponent values (all p under .014). None of the additional demographic and clinical variables improved model fit beyond age and sex (all p under.143). After adjustment for age and sex, neither offset (p=.898) nor exponent (p=.100) differed between patients and controls. Conclusion: Resting-state aperiodic EEG parameters were consistently associated with age and sex, but not with self-reported symptom burden or clinical characteristics in patients with PPCS. Not accounting for these factors may generate apparent group differences attributable, at least in part, to demographic variability. Significance: Age and sex are important sources of inter-individual variability in resting-state aperiodic EEG activity and should be systematically considered when investigating such features.

papers.title: Genetic susceptibility to Lewy body disease and the distribution of Lewy pathology
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies of Parkinsons disease and dementia with Lewy bodies largely rely on clinical diagnoses, which can misclassify cases and cannot characterise the anatomical distribution of Lewy pathology. Autopsy cohorts allow identification of variants associated both with developing Lewy body disease and with the neocortical extent of its pathology. We meta-analysed genome-wide data from 2,661 individuals of European ancestry with autopsy-confirmed Lewy body disease and 12,068 controls (2,124 autopsy-confirmed) from the Global Parkinsons Genetics Program (GP2) and the National Institutes of Health NeuroBioBank, and estimated genetic correlation with clinically diagnosed Alzheimers disease. In 2,309 cases from the GP2 and the Mayo Clinic Jacksonville Brain Bank, we compared neocortical (n = 1,362) with brainstem or limbic (n = 947) Lewy pathology, adjusting for Alzheimers disease co-pathology, age at death and sex. Under a neuropathological case definition, five established loci reached genome-wide significance: APOE4 (OR 2.27, 95% CI 2.06-2.50), GBA1 E326K (OR 2.57, 95% CI 2.01-3.28), SNCA (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.23-1.48; TMEM175 p.M393T (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.19-1.43), and HLA class II (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.61-0.79). Lead associations differed by antemortem diagnosis. Across all cases, the SNCA association was indexed by a 5 signal previously associated with dementia with Lewy bodies and rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder, rather than the canonical 3 Parkinsons disease variant. Among 1,216 cases diagnosed during life with Parkinsons disease, with or without dementia, the 3 variant was the lead SNCA signal, and the APOE4 effect was attenuated (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37-1.81). Genetic correlation with Alzheimers disease (0.33, P = 0.02) persisted after excluding the APOE region (0.31, P = 0.03). Within cases, APOE4 was the only susceptibility locus associated with neocortical involvement (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.45-1.98; P = 2.5 x 10-11), including among 666 GP2 cases without significant Alzheimers disease co-pathology (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.18-2.63; P = 0.005). Each additional e4 allele was also associated with a more advanced Lewy pathology stage (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.50-2.06). Autopsy-confirmed Lewy body disease shares its major susceptibility loci with clinically defined disease. Of these, only APOE4 was also associated with neocortical involvement, independently of measured Alzheimers disease co-pathology, suggesting that it influences not only whether Lewy pathology develops but how far it extends.

papers.title: Racial Disparities and Trends in Alzheimers and Parkinsons Disease-Related Mortality: A CDC WONDER Study 2018-2024
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective: The objectives of this study were to examine racial differences and temporal trends in Alzheimer's disease (AD)- and Parkinson's disease (PD)-related mortality among U.S. adults and to assess whether racial mortality patterns and temporal changes differed. Methods: We analyzed CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data from 2018-2024, where mortality was defined as deaths with AD or PD recorded as an underlying or contributing cause. Age-standardized mortality rates and adjusted mortality rate ratios (MRRs) were estimated. Joint-point regression evaluated racial differences, annual percentage changes (APCs), and disease-race-year interactions. Sensitivity analyses assessed the robustness of the findings. Results: Black had significantly lower PD-related mortality than White (adjusted mortality rate ratios [MRRs]: 0.62-0.69; all p<0.001), whereas AD-related mortality showed no significant racial differences (MRRs: 0.91-1.06). Compared with 2018, mortality increased significantly in 2020 for both diseases among White adults (AD: MRR=1.21; PD: MRR=1.27) and Black adults (AD: MRR=1.27; PD: MRR=1.37), followed by partial declines. PD-related mortality increased significantly among White adults during 2018-2023 (annual percentage change [APC]=3.08%; 95% CI: 1.15%-5.05%), whereas trends among Black adults (APC=3.51%; 95% CI: -2.94% to 10.39%) and AD-related mortality trends in both racial groups were not statistically significant. The disease-race-year interaction was not significant (p=0.942), indicating insufficient evidence that temporal mortality patterns differed jointly. Conclusions: Recorded PD-related mortality was lower among Black than White adults, whereas AD-related mortality showed no statistically significant racial difference. These findings support disease-specific mortality surveillance and further investigation of potential differences in diagnostic recognition and death-certificate documentation.

papers.title: A digital biomarker of white-matter routing from diffusion MRI as an early biomarker of Alzheimer's disease
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is diagnosed after a decade-long phase in which pathology accumulates; current markers show that pathology is present, but not how far it has advanced. Because white-matter structure is altered early, we computed two graph-theoretic indices of periventricular white-matter routing from diffusion MRI in 1,706 OASIS-3 sessions: the Route Concordance Index (RCI), a population-calibrated path-concordance score over 316 routes, and a global conductance from the connectome's graph Laplacian. RCI was reduced before clinical conversion and declined monotonically across a five-stage trajectory (cross-validated AUC = 0.817 for stable-CN vs. pre-AD; comparable to hippocampal volume and exceeding entorhinal thickness, global conductance, and DTI-ALPS), with degradation concentrated in fronto-striatal circuits. A classifier combining these routing features with demographic, structural-MRI and cognitive covariates detected conversion to MCI or AD up to four years before diagnosis (AUC = 0.831; 0.918 within one year; modest positive predictive value). Findings replicated in ADNI (n = 609; conductance AUC = 0.805; RCI = 0.797 under frozen external validation) and tracked CSF amyloid-beta 42 in the expected direction. Computed from a standard diffusion MRI sequence, RCI is comparable to established structural and demographic biomarkers on preclinical discrimination while, unlike them, declining cleanly and monotonically across the disease trajectory, supporting prospective validation for risk stratification.

papers.title: Plasma Proteomic Correlates of Cognitive Function in Older Adults From Central Africa
papers.abstract: Importance: Blood based proteomic biomarkers may support scalable dementia research, but their associations with cognitive phenotype remain poorly characterized in sub Saharan African populations. Objective: To examine associations between selected plasma proteins and multidomain cognitive performance in older adults in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Design: Cross sectional secondary analysis of baseline data from the Etude du Vieillissement Cognitif et de Demence en Republique Democratique du Congo (EVCD RDC), with participant recruitment and data collection from July 2024 through September 2025. Setting: Community based prospective cohort in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Participants: The analytic sample included 779 participants: 143 cognitively unimpaired, 218 with mild cognitive impairment, 203 with Alzheimer disease, and 215 with other dementia. Median age was 73 years (IQR, 70 to 78); 495 participants (63.5%) were female and 284 (36.5%) were male. Exposures: Plasma abundance of 10 candidate proteins measured using the NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120. Candidates were selected from an earlier panel wide analysis based on cognitively unimpaired vs Alzheimer disease discrimination and false discovery rate adjusted significance. Main Outcomes and Measures: Seven cognitive outcomes spanning global cognition, language, working memory, learning, delayed memory, mental abstraction, and problem solving. Separate linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, current smoking, education, and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Benjamini Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied within each cognitive outcome across the 10 proteins. Results: Eighteen protein cognition associations were nominally significant, and 6 remained significant after correction. Higher MME was associated with better language, global cognition, and delayed memory. Higher NEFL was associated with poorer global cognition and delayed memory. Higher ENO2 was associated with better delayed memory. No p tau217 based measure remained significant after correction. Conclusions and Relevance: MME and NEFL showed the most consistent associations with cognitive performance, whereas ptau217 based measures did not survive multiple testing correction. Biomarkers optimized for Alzheimer pathology detection may differ from those most closely associated with cross sectional cognitive phenotype, supporting population specific evaluation of plasma proteomic markers.

papers.title: Cognitive Trajectories of Post-Stroke Delirium: Longitudinal Global and Domain-Specific Impairment and Digital Markers
papers.abstract: Background: Poststroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) and poststroke delirium (PSD) remain underexplored. Longitudinal assessments of cognition before PSD onset and at follow-up are scarce, leaving the association between PSD and subsequent global and domain-specific PSCI unclear. Digital assessments using task-derived kinematic parameters may provide complementary insights into cognitive vulnerability and PSD risk. Methods: In this prospective longitudinal study, patients with acute stroke underwent multidomain tablet-based neuropsychological assessment within the acute phase, before PSD onset, and at 90 days post-stroke. Global PSCI (gPSCI) and domain-specific PSCI (attention and processing speed, executive functions, verbal memory, language, and visuospatial-construction) were assessed using norm-referenced cognitive performance. Cognitive outcomes were compared between patients with and without PSD at both time points. Functional outcome, mortality, and quality of life were assessed at 90 days. Exploratory random forest analyses evaluated the discriminatory ability of acute-phase task-derived kinematic parameters. Results: Among 31 patients with stroke, 10 developed PSD, 18 served as controls, and 3 dropped out. At 90 days, patients with PSD had more severe gPSCI than controls (U=19.500, p<0.001), whereas the acute-phase difference was not significant (U=50.500, p=0.057). Domain-specific analyses revealed distinct temporal patterns of cognitive impairment. During the acute phase, patients with subsequent PSD, showed significantly more severe impairments in attention and processing speed (U=29.500; p=0.003) and visuospatial-construction (U=31.500; p=0.004). At 90 days, differences in attention and processing speed persisted (U=21.000, p <0.001) with additional significant differences in executive functions (U=38.500, p=0.012) and language (U=45.500, p=0.031). Kinematic parameters showed discriminatory performance comparable to gPSCI (78.89% versus 81.50%). At 90 days, PSD was also associated with worse functional outcome (U=31.500, p=0.004), higher mortality (p=0.037), and lower mental quality of life (p=0.021). Conclusions: PSD is associated with more severe global PSCI at 90 days post-stroke and distinct temporal pattern of domain-specific PSCI. Task-derived kinematic parameters may complement conventional cognitive scores. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings.

papers.title: Radiological Phenotypes of Acute Brain Injury During Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation on Ultra-Low-Field Portable MRI
papers.abstract: Background: Despite the clinical importance of acute brain injury (ABI) during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), the mechanism of ECMO-associated ABI remains poorly understood, partly because conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is incompatible with ECMO devices. Ultra-low-field portable MRI (ULF-pMRI) enables high-quality bedside neuroimaging during ECMO. We aimed to characterize imaging phenotypes of ABI and explore mechanisms underlying lesion distribution across ECMO configurations. Methods: In this multicenter retrospective observational study, adults receiving ECMO who underwent bedside ULF-pMRI at Johns Hopkins University and University of Texas?Houston from December 2021 to May 2026 were included. ABI was defined as ischemic stroke (IS), intraparenchymal hemorrhage (IPH), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), or subdural hematoma (SDH). Lesions were characterized according to vascular territory, cortical/subcortical lesion versus deep white matter (WM)/basal ganglia (BG) involvement, laterality, lesion burden, and cerebral small-vessel disease (SVD) using Fazekas scale. Associations between ECMO configuration (central venoarterial [VA], peripheral VA, and venovenous [VV]), echocardiographic findings, and ECMO parameters were examined. Results: Among 70 patients analyzed (55.9 {+/-} 16.2 years; 54.3% male), 29 (41.4%) had ABI. IS was the predominant type of ABI (82.8%), with most strokes affecting the frontal lobe (48.3%). All the central VA-ECMO patients with ABI demonstrated predominantly cortical/subcortical lesions, whereas deep WM/BG involvement was more frequent in peripheral VA-ECMO (53.8%). Peripheral VA-ECMO demonstrated left hemispheric predominance (85% vs. 15% right-sided, P=0.002), and deep WM/BG lesions in peripheral were associated with higher ECMO pump flow and lower pulse pressure. Among VV-ECMO patients, bilateral lesions were more common (62.5%), with a high prevalence of deep WM/BG involvement (62.5%) and SVD (75%). Conclusions: ULF-pMRI revealed distinct radiological phenotypes of ABI across ECMO configurations; cortical/subcortical lesions in central VA-ECMO, left-sided predominance in peripheral VA-ECMO and frequent deep WM/BG in VV-ECMO. These findings generate mechanistic hypotheses regarding configuration-specific pathways of ABI.

papers.title: Greater scaling and less flexible timing of cortical responses during challenging reactive balance after stroke
papers.abstract: Background: Cortical N1 responses to balance perturbations are larger and earlier with increasing magnitude and differ with reactive stepping. Whether stroke alters this modulation is unknown. Objective: To compare N1 modulation across perturbation magnitudes and reactive balance outcomes in older adults with and without stroke. We hypothesized that people with stroke would show greater N1 scaling than controls; that larger N1s at small perturbations would limit scaling (a recruitment ceiling); and that stroke would constrain N1 modulation by stepping outcome. Methods: Sixteen people with chronic stroke (66+/-11 years) and 15 age-similar controls (68+/-8 years) received forward support-surface perturbations at a small standardized magnitude and at individual step thresholds (~50% unintentional steps). N1 peak amplitude and latency were compared across magnitudes in feet-in-place trials, and between stepping and feet-in-place trials at step threshold. N1 scaling was the relative amplitude increase between magnitudes. Results: Despite lower clinical balance after stroke (p<0.001), step thresholds were similar between groups. N1s were larger with shorter latencies at step threshold in both groups (p<0.001), but scaled more after stroke (44% vs 13%,p=0.009). Greater scaling was associated with smaller small-magnitude N1s after stroke (B=0.43, p=0.041) and higher step thresholds across groups (B=0.35, p=0.048). N1 latency was 11 ms longer in stepping trials in controls but not after stroke (interaction p=0.024). Conclusions: Scaling of cortical recruitment with increasing perturbation magnitude may support reactive balance, and may be an adaptive mechanism for people after stroke. Less flexible N1 timing after stroke may limit cortical tuning to balance recovery strategy.

papers.title: Live Birth Rates Among Women With Multiple Sclerosis in Sweden, 2004 to 2022: A Population-Based Registry Study
papers.abstract: Background: Women with multiple sclerosis (MS) have fewer children than other women, but whether this narrowed as pregnancy evidence became reassuring and treatment options expanded is uncertain. Objective: To compare live birth trends from 2004 to 2022 between women with MS and all Swedish women. Methods: Linking the Swedish MS, National Patient, and Medical Birth Registers with national statistics, we compared age-standardised live birth rates, counted expected births at national rates, and estimated adjusted annual live-birth risk ratios in a matched comparison sample. Results: Women with MS (n=10,452; 76,989 woman-years) had 3,577 children, about 1,200 (25%) fewer than expected (observed-to-expected ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.72 to 0.77). Standardised rate ratios were below 1 annually (median 0.77). Observed-to-expected ratios were 0.73 (0.68 to 0.79) in 2004 to 2008 and 0.70 (0.65 to 0.75) in 2019 to 2022 (population-by-period interaction p=0.31). Age- and region-adjusted risk ratios ranged from 0.75 to 0.86 across periods (heterogeneity p=0.020), closest to 1 in 2009 to 2013. Conclusion: Women with MS had about one quarter fewer live births than other Swedish women, and the difference was similar in the first and last periods.

papers.title: Hormone Replacement Therapy and Disability Progression in Women with Multiple Sclerosis
papers.abstract: Background: Evidence on menopausal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and disability progression in women with multiple sclerosis (MS) is limited, particularly in the era of high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy. We estimated the association between systemic HRT and sustained disability progression and recurring relapses in a contemporary national cohort. Methods: In a nationwide Swedish registry-based cohort, we followed women with MS aged 40 to 60 years entering from 2006 through 2024, with follow-up through 2025, under a new-user design. Systemic HRT was modeled as time-varying current use and quarterly oral-equivalent dose categories. Outcomes were sustained Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) 4.0, sustained EDSS 6.0, and recurring relapses. Cox models adjusted for baseline covariates and time-varying age and disease-modifying therapy (DMT) class. Results: Among 7,623 women, 1,192 (15.6%) initiated HRT. Current HRT use was associated with a lower hazard of sustained EDSS 4.0 (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.70, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51 to 0.96) but not sustained EDSS 6.0 (aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.16) or recurring relapses (aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.36). Dose categories showed no consistent gradient. Raising the cohort-entry age floor to 50 years gave a consistent EDSS 4.0 estimate (aHR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.95). Conclusions: HRT was not associated with increased relapse risk or severe disability progression. The lower hazard of sustained EDSS 4.0 was not mirrored at EDSS 6.0 and showed no dose gradient. Given menopausal status was unmeasured, replication in cohorts with verified menopausal status is required for clear clinical interpretation.

papers.title: More tests, higher scores: Testing frequency and SDMT differences between natalizumab and rituximab
papers.abstract: Background: The Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) measures information processing speed, and repeated testing can increase scores through practice effects. However, how differences in testing frequency bear on comparisons between disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) in real-world cohorts has not been fully explored. Objective: To compare SDMT trajectories between natalizumab and rituximab users and quantify the association of the testing process with those trajectories. Methods: Using the Swedish MS Registry, we studied adults with relapsing-remitting MS initiating natalizumab or rituximab (2010-2024) with >=2 on-treatment SDMT assessments. Mixed-effects models with restricted cubic spline time were sequentially adjusted; log cumulative test number was the practice-effect adjustment. Results: Among 2,458 individuals, natalizumab initiators were tested twice as often as rituximab initiators (1.6 vs. 0.8 tests/year). The predicted natalizumab-minus-rituximab SDMT difference at 3 years was 7.0 points (95% CI 5.7-8.3) unadjusted and 1.6 (0.7-2.6) after full adjustment including cumulative test number; at 1 year it fell from 4.4 (3.3-5.4) to -0.3 (-1.2 to 0.6). Conclusion: Adjustment for cumulative test number substantially attenuated the SDMT difference between natalizumab and rituximab, leaving a small residual difference of uncertain clinical importance and underscoring the need to account for testing frequency in real-world comparisons.

papers.title: Characterization of Sleep, Spectral, and Epileptiform Activity in Individuals Aged 8-27 Years with SYNGAP1-Related Disorder Using an at-Home Dry EEG Headband
papers.abstract: SYNGAP1-related disorder (SYNGAP1-RD) is associated with sleep disturbances, seizures, and neurophysiological abnormalities. However, in-lab EEG can be difficult to obtain due to the behavioral and sensory disorders associated with this condition. In this study we collected EEG in SYNGAP1-RD participants (n=30 enrolled, 27 contributing data) in a decentralized protocol using a dry electrode headband as a path to longitudinal, research-grade data collection in this population. At-home data collection was successful with 180 recordings containing over 1 hour of usable data collected from 23 participants. Across these recordings, sporadic interictal epileptiform discharges were present in 22 of 23 participants but electrographic seizures were not observed. Relative to an adolescent control population (n=10), SYNGAP1-RD participants showed increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, and decreased time in N1 and N3 sleep stages along with increased time in N2. We reproduced prior findings from awake spectral EEG analyses, including elevated broadband power along with reduced relative alpha power and alpha-theta ratio in the SYNGAP1 cohort. Notably, differences in spectral power were tightly linked to sleep stage, revealing sleep-stage-dependent spectral biomarker dynamics not previously characterized in SYNGAP1-RD. Finally, we examined differences between variants producing truncations downstream of the GAP domain and those producing truncations before or within it, but analyses were limited by a small sample size (n=4 for the post-GAP variant). Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of at-home multi-night sleep EEG collection in participants with SYNGAP1-RD and led to both corroborative and novel findings.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Rett Syndrome: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Explainable AI
papers.abstract: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by abnormal cortical activity, which can be captured using electroencephalography (EEG). Although machine learning (ML) has shown promise for diagnosing several neurological conditions, comprehensive evaluation of classical ML and deep learning (DL) methods, together with physiologically meaningful explanations, remains limited for RTT. This study analyses resting-state, eyes-closed EEG recordings from RTT patients and healthy controls using both power spectral density (PSD)-based ML and end-to-end DL frameworks. Classical ML models, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were trained on PSD features, while EEG-specific DL architectures, including ShallowConvNet, DeepConvNet, EEGNet, and EEG Conformer, were trained directly on preprocessed EEG signals. Subject-wise cross-validation was used to avoid data leakage, with balanced accuracy as the primary performance metric because it equally accounts for sensitivity and specificity. Random Forest achieved the best performance among the classical ML models, whereas EEGNet achieved the highest DL performance. An ablation study indicated that 4-second EEG epochs offered the optimal trade-off between model performance and robustness. Model interpretability was investigated using SHAP for Random Forest and occlusion sensitivity analysis for EEGNet. Both methods consistently identified delta and theta oscillations, along with centro-frontal brain regions, as key contributors to RTT classification. These findings show that both PSD-based machine learning and end-to-end deep learning methods can reliably identify RTT and highlight common neurophysiological biomarkers, offering an interpretable framework for EEG-based diagnosis and biomarker discovery for Rett Syndrome.

papers.title: Cortical physiological arousal following termination of absence seizures
papers.abstract: Although the brain state preceding and during absence seizures has been well-characterized, the postictal brain state remains largely unexplored due to the prevailing assumption that absence seizures have minimal or no postictal changes. To address this gap, scalp EEG recordings from 55 patients with 3-4 Hz spike-wave discharges across four multi-site cohorts were analyzed. Spectral power was measured relative to each seizure's preictal baseline, and the postictal period was compared to a time-matched preictal window. Rather than an immediate return to baseline after seizure offset, a significant broadband increase in EEG power was observed in the gamma (>25 Hz) and delta (<4 Hz) frequency bands, followed by a gradual decline over the next 15 s to 30 s. In contrast, no comparable change preceded the seizures. This suggests that recovery from an absence seizure is an active process with a characteristic electrophysiological signature consistent with cortical activation and arousal. Thus, postictal arousal may facilitate exit from the seizure state, and with further work could serve as an electrophysiological marker and therapeutic target for recovery in absence epilepsy.

papers.title: Glymphatic Dysfunction Across Sleep Disorders and Its Cognitive Implications
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), sleep deprivation (SD), and narcolepsy type 1 (NT1), are associated with cognitive dysfunction and an increased risk of neurodegenerative disease. Glymphatic transport disruption has been suggested as one potential mechanistic link. However, evidence across sleep disorders and glymphatic-related metrics remains fragmented. We aimed to determine whether glymphatic-related metrics are altered in OSA, SD, and NT1. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical and preclinical studies to determine whether glymphatic-related metrics are altered in OSA, SD, and NT1. Across studies of OSA, glymphatic-related metrics indicated significant impairment of glymphatic transport with a moderate negative association between apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) and diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index (r=-0.53, 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.63 to -0.41; p<0.001). Available evidence did not demonstrate statistically significant alterations in glymphatic measures in SD or NT1. These findings suggest that impaired glymphatic transport may represent a potential pathway linking OSA to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative risk. However, current evidence is insufficient to determine whether comparable alterations occur in SD or NT1. Substantial heterogeneity across studies highlights the need for standardized reporting and harmonized methodologies to advance the field.

papers.title: Movement-specific effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation over premotor and parietal cortices after stroke
papers.abstract: Background: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has been proposed to support post-stroke motor recovery, but the response may depend on the task and motor-network status. We aimed to compare how premotor and parietal stimulation affects performance across reach directions with different movement demands, in preparation for therapeutic application of TMS. Methods: 16 participants with chronic subcortical stroke performed planar reaches with the KINARM exoskeleton toward distal and proximal targets. Before movement, a 10-Hz triple-pulse TMS train was delivered over bilateral dorsal or ventral premotor cortex (PMd, PMv) or dorsomedial posterior parietal cortex (PPC) at subthreshold and suprathreshold intensities. The parietal midline was used as the control target. Participant-level bootstrap confidence intervals assessed changes in trajectory straightness and smoothness relative to the control target and differences between reach directions. We compared motor-network activity and connectivity using task-based and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from participants with stroke and neurologically intact controls. To explore response variability, we tested associations between TMS response and motor impairment, resting-state connectivity, and the change in task-evoked activity at the stimulated region from planning to movement. Results: Suprathreshold PMd and PPC stimulation in both hemispheres improved trajectory straightness or smoothness during distal reaches relative to the control target. Suprathreshold contralesional PMd stimulation increased trajectory deviation and reduced smoothness during proximal reaches. Baseline performance during distal reaches was more closely related to motor impairment, and contralesional PMd effects were more favorable during distal than proximal reaches across all kinematic measures. Participants with stroke showed lower bilateral PMv activation during movement and stronger interhemispheric PPC connectivity. Only the change in task-evoked activity at the stimulated region from planning to movement was related to TMS response. Smaller changes relative to controls were associated with more favorable kinematic effects during distal reaches. Conclusions: Movements more affected after stroke were the most responsive to this type of stimulation. The response to TMS was also associated with task-evoked activity differences at the stimulated region between movement planning and execution. Neuromodulation may therefore be most effective when designed around both the pathophysiology of the cortical target and the type of movement.

papers.title: Amyloid and Tau Neuropathologic Stage, Coexisting Brain Disease, and Cognitive Status in a Population-Based Autopsy Cohort
papers.abstract: Importance: Interpreting an amyloid or tau biomarker result requires knowing how often the target pathology is present in the tested population, whether a single marker characterizes the joint amyloid-tau state, and whether the detected pathology explains the patient symptoms. Population-based autopsy data addressing these questions are scarce, and recent population-scale prevalence estimates rest on biomarkers rather than ground-truth tissue examination. Objective: To estimate stage-resolved, age- and sex-specific frequencies of amyloid and tau neuropathology in an unselected, admixed, autopsy population and to evaluate their clinical expression in relation to coexisting neuropathology. Design Setting and Participants: Cross-sectional clinicopathologic study of decedents accrued from 2004 through 2025 at the Biobank for Aging Studies of the University of Sao Paulo, sampled through the centralized Sao Paulo municipal autopsy service, which performs approximately 15 000 autopsies annually and verifies about 16% of deaths in the city. Eligible decedents were aged 18 years or older with complete amyloid, tau, Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR), and coexisting pathology assessments. Exposures: Age, sex, Thal amyloid phase, Braak neurofibrillary tangle stage, Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer Disease (CERAD) neuritic plaque score, and contributing coexisting neuropathology. Main Outcomes and Measures: The complete Thal phase by Braak stage distribution; age- and sex-specific frequency of pathology in the biomarker-detectable range, prespecified as Thal phase 3 to 5 together with Braak stage IV to VI; and associations with CDR and CDR Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB). Results: Among 2711 decedents (mean [SD] age, 73.4 [14.4] years; range, 23 to 111 years; 1340 [49.4%] female), 531 (19.6%) met both thresholds, 270 (10.0%) the amyloid threshold only, 207 (7.6%) the tau threshold only, and 1703 (62.8%) neither. Frequency of the combined state rose from 0% at ages 23 to 50 years to 5.5% at 61 to 70, 14.5% at 71 to 80, 36.5% at 81 to 90, and 45.9% at 91 to 111 years. The proportion with CDR greater than 0 increased monotonically across Braak stages, from 88 of 541 (16.3%) at stage 0 to 155 of 179 (86.6%) at stage VI. When the combined amyloid-tau state was cross-classified with contributing coexisting pathology, CDR greater than 0 was present in 225 of 1467 participants (15.3%) with neither, 204 of 349 (58.5%) with coexisting pathology alone, 216 of 339 (63.7%) with combined amyloid-tau pathology alone, and 165 of 192 (85.9%) with both. In a multivariable model of CDR-SB, contributing coexisting pathology had the largest unique adjusted contribution (partial R2, 0.088; 95% CI, 0.064-0.114), and Braak stage had the largest share of total explained variance (Lindeman, Merenda, and Gold contribution, 0.115). Conclusions and Relevance: Amyloid and tau pathology within the range detected by current biomarkers was uncommon before age 70 and discordant in 17.6% of decedents. Contributing coexisting brain disease, which amyloid and tau biomarkers do not detect, accompanied cognitive impairment as often as advanced Alzheimer disease pathology did. These tissue-based frequencies can inform the interpretation of positive and negative biomarker results.

papers.title: High-Density Surface Electromyography Detects Fiber-Type-Related Profiles and Disease-Relevant Fatigue Trajectories in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
papers.abstract: Fiber-type composition contributes to contractile behavior and fatigue resistance. Characterizing these physiological differences could help study and monitor disease-related changes. Direct fiber-type measurement requires biopsy, whereas animal findings may not fully translate to humans. High-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG) may offer repeatable, noninvasive assessment. We recorded HD-sEMG from tibialis anterior (TA) and soleus, muscles with contrasting fast- and slow-twitch-like physiology, during sustained contractions at 30% and 50% maximum voluntary contraction in participants with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS; n = 7) and healthy controls (n = 10). Given fast-fatigable motor unit vulnerability in ALS models, we compared TA-soleus profiles and fatigue-related changes. Amplitude, spectral, motor unit firing, and motor unit action potential (MUAP) features were quantified in the first 10 s of stable contraction, with firing and MUAP features derived from decomposition. Exploratory fatigue analyses assessed early-to-late changes and trajectories. Early-window root mean square (RMS), spectral power, firing rate, and MUAP amplitude were higher in TA than soleus in both groups. Group x Muscle interactions were nonsignificant. Despite higher early values, TA showed larger fatigue-related declines in high-frequency power, RMS, and firing rate than soleus, particularly in ALS-affected TA. These findings suggest HD-sEMG detects muscle-type-related electrophysiological differences, with ALS-related changes more evident during fatigue.

papers.title: APOLLAI, a multimodal AI system, versus EMS personnel for prehospital detection of stroke-related deficits
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose: Prehospital stroke recognition remains suboptimal, with nearly one-third of strokes unidentified before hospital arrival, and neurological assessment being inherently subjective, with substantial interobserver variability even among certified clinicians. APOLLAI, a multimodal artificial intelligence system, was developed to detect stroke-related neurological deficits from video and audio recordings. We compared the diagnostic performance of APOLLAI and emergency medical services (EMS) personnel against an expert consensus reference standard. Methods: In this prospective study, video recordings of 295 patients with suspected stroke (mean age, 70.3 {+/-}13.3 years) were obtained at Nimes University Hospital (August 2023-July 2025). Five National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale items (best gaze, facial palsy, motor arm, aphasia, dysarthria) were independently annotated by seven certified stroke neurologists, combined into consensus labels using the Dawid-Skene algorithm, and separately assessed by EMS personnel (mean of 15 raters per patient). APOLLAI, a multimodal machine-learning framework that combines computer vision, audio-based deep learning, and a final support vector machine (SVM) fusion classifier, was evaluated against EMS using sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results: Interrater agreement among the seven neurologists was moderate overall (mean {kappa}=0.541, range, 0.367-0.732), indicating an intrinsic difficulty of neurological assessment. APOLLAI showed higher sensitivity than EMS for all five neurological tasks and for the global assessment (78.5% versus 59.4%), with broadly comparable specificity (87.0% versus 85.9% for the global assessment). AUC values ranged from 0.839 (facial palsy) to 0.966 (best gaze), with a global AUC of 0.882. Conclusions: APOLLAI demonstrated higher sensitivity than EMS personnel for detecting stroke-related neurological deficits, with preserved specificity. These findings support its potential as a standardized, scalable adjunct to prehospital stroke recognition, warranting prospective validation under real-world EMS conditions.

papers.title: Plasma Proteomic Classification of Alzheimer Disease, Parkinson Disease, and Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Using a Single Neurodegeneration Panel: A Diagnostic Cohort Study
papers.abstract: ImportanceBlood biomarkers for Alzheimer disease(AD), Parkinson disease(PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis(ALS) are typically developed as disease-specific single-analyte tests. Whether one shared plasma panel can support disease-selective classification remains unclear. ObjectiveTo test whether the Olink Target 48 Neurodegeneration plasma panel, analyzed with disease-specific Elastic Net models, can discriminate AD, PD, and ALS in a heterogeneous neurological cohort. Design, Setting, and ParticipantsSingle-center diagnostic cohort study at Keio University Hospital, Tokyo, Japan. After quality control and one consent withdrawal, 302 participants were analyzed(healthy controls n = 62; AD continuum n = 93; PD n = 39; ALS n = 27; other neurological disorders n = 81) and allocated by diagnosis-stratified sampling into a discovery training set(n = 211) and a locked hold-out test set(n = 91). ExposuresPlasma normalized protein expression from 42 assays retained after protein quality control. Plasma DOPA decarboxylase was excluded a priori from all classifiers because blood levels primarily reflect dopaminergic treatment exposure. Main Outcomes and MeasuresHold-out receiver operating characteristic area under the curve(AUC). Sensitivity and specificity at a training-set Youden threshold locked for Test. ResultsHold-out AUCs were 0.974(95% CI, 0.942-0.995) for AD, 0.926(0.820-1.000) for PD, and 0.995(0.980-1.000) for ALS. At locked Youden cutoffs, sensitivity was 0.929 (95% CI, 0.765-0.991) and specificity was 0.921 (95% CI, 0.824-0.974) for AD, 0.833 (95% CI, 0.516-0.979) and 0.975 (95% CI, 0.912-0.997) for PD, and 1.000 (95% CI, 0.631-1.000) and 0.940 (95% CI, 0.865-0.980) for ALS. Conclusions and RelevanceA single plasma neurodegeneration panel supported disease-selective classification of AD, PD, and ALS in internal validation. Multicenter external validation is needed before clinical application. Key PointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSCan a single plasma neurodegeneration panel classify Alzheimer disease (AD), Parkinson disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in a heterogeneous neurological cohort? FindingsIn this diagnostic cohort study, disease-specific Elastic Net models derived from a single plasma panel enabled the discrimination of AD, PD, and ALS from other neurological disorders and healthy controls. MeaningA single plasma neurodegeneration panel can simultaneously support disease-selective classification of AD, PD, and ALS, offering a unified approach to blood-based diagnosis.

papers.title: Sensorimotor cortex activity during cued gait differs in Parkinson's freezers and non-freezers
papers.abstract: Gait impairments are a major contributor to disability in patients with Parkinsons disease despite dopaminergic and neuromodulation therapies. External cues (e.g., visual targets, rhythmic auditory sounds) are commonly used to improve gait quality and reduce freezing of gait (FOG), yet their effectiveness varies across patients and contexts. Improved understanding of the neural mechanisms of cueing benefits is essential to personalize rehabilitation strategies and improve outcomes. We use mobile electroencephalography (EEG) to test the hypothesis that cues improve gait through engagement of voluntary motor control mechanisms to compensate for impaired gait automaticity. In addition, we investigate whether this mechanism is related to cueing benefits or freezing status. Eighteen PD patients with a history of freezing (PD-F), 21 patients without freezing (PD-NF) and 19 age-matched healthy controls (HC) walked overground under three conditions: normal walking, synchronizing to auditory cues, and stepping over visual cues. Stride-locked beta band (13-30 Hz) power dynamics in sensorimotor cortex were used to measure cortical control of stepping. Spatiotemporal gait parameters improved with cues in all groups. However, PD-F had smaller cue-related gains in speed and stride length when compared with PD-NF for both cue types, and did not improve gait speed with visual cues. EEG revealed greater contralateral sensorimotor cortex swing-phase beta suppression in PD-F than PD-NF patients, with visual cues eliciting the most robust response. In contrast, beta suppression with cues was less pronounced in PD-NF and HC, despite greater behavioral gains. In addition, engagement of sensorimotor cortex during visual cueing was associated with divergent gait effects across PD subgroups: In PD-NF greater beta suppression was associated with less gait improvement, whereas in PD-F the opposite was observed. These findings suggest distinct sensorimotor control mechanisms for cue utilization in PD-F and PD-NF, and indicate that engagement of voluntary motor control circuits may underlie cueing benefits primarily in PD-F.

papers.title: Near infrared spectroscopy during non-ischaemic handgrip exercise reveals divergent muscle oxygenation signatures in mitochondrial disease and sarcopenia
papers.abstract: Background: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of ageing and is implicated in the pathogenesis of sarcopenia. Genetically confirmed mitochondrial disease provides a biologically definitive model of impaired oxidative phosphorylation against which novel functional assessments can be validated. We investigated whether a brief, submaximal, non-ischaemic intermittent isometric handgrip exercise protocol combined with Near Infra-Red Spectroscopy (NIRS) could detect distinct muscle oxygenation signatures in mitochondrial disease and sarcopenia. Methods: Adults with genetically confirmed mitochondrial disease (n=10, 7 female) and group-matched controls (n=19, 11 female), underwent assessment of maximal grip force, handgrip relaxation kinetics and a 3-minute intermittent submaximal isometric handgrip test (40% maximal voluntary contraction, 1Hz contraction/relaxation) with continuous force recording at 2000Hz and simultaneous NIRS. Findings were compared with 23 community-dwelling older adults from the Muscle Ageing and Sarcopenia Study (MASS) Lifecourse cohort (n=23, 13 female) including seven with probable or confirmed sarcopenia according to European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP2) criteria. Results: Participants with mitochondrial disease demonstrated an attenuated reduction in tissue saturation index (TSI) during exercise compared with controls (TSI % {middle dot} s150-180s: -59.9 {+/-} 94.5 vs -175.1 {+/-} 128.4; p=0.02). Total haemoglobin (THb) responses did not differ between groups (p=0.10). In contrast, participants with probable or confirmed sarcopenia showed exaggerated reduction in TSI compared with non-sarcopenic participants (TSI % {middle dot} s150-180s: -256.5 {+/-} 146.0 vs -121.2 {+/-} 95.2; p=0.05), while THb responses remained similar. The association between sarcopenia and TSI differed by sex (interaction coefficient -240, p=0.016), with greater TSI reductions observed in males with sarcopenia. Differences in TSI between mitochondrial disease and control groups were independent of age and sex. No statistically significant associations were observed between THb responses and age, sex or force production. Conclusions: A brief, non-ischaemic handgrip exercise protocol combined with NIRS identified divergent muscle oxygenation responses in mitochondrial disease and sarcopenia. The attenuated TSI response observed in genetically confirmed mitochondrial disease is consistent with impaired oxygen utilisation secondary to defective oxidative phosphorylation, whereas the exaggerated TSI reduction observed in sarcopenia suggests a distinct physiological mechanism, potentially involving impaired oxygen delivery, reduced muscle efficiency, or both. This portable and non-invasive approach has significant potential as a physiological biomarker for mechanistic studies and clinical trials in ageing and neuromuscular disease. More broadly, our findings demonstrate how biologically defined rare diseases can provide a powerful framework for interpreting mechanisms in common heterogeneous age-related conditions.

papers.title: AI Tools to Assist with Management of Patient Portal Messages: Auto-Categorization and Routing
papers.abstract: Background and ObjectiveThe volume of patient portal messages has grown substantially and artificial intelligence (AI) can support clinical staff and improve the timeliness of patient care. Our objective is to test if an AI tool for managing the electronic inbox "In-Basket" reduces response times to patient portal messages in neurology. MethodsWe conducted an implementation study from January to May 2026 in the neurology department at two clinical sites within a regional medical system. A single AI tool was implemented to auto-categorize and auto-route all patient messages received in the electronic inbox. The tool also generates optional draft replies to messages. Primary process measures were the median weekly time (hours) from message creation to the first action and to closure. Impact was analyzed using a controlled interrupted time-series (ITS) design, comparing message-volume-matched control divisions. ResultsAmong 24,142 messages analyzed, pre-intervention median weekly time to first action was 11.3 hours [IQR: 5.6, 15.1] (Site A) and 16.1 hours [IQR: 13.8, 19.0] (Site B), falling post-intervention to 1.0 hour [IQR: 0, 3.1] (Site A) and 0.6 hours [IQR: 0.2, 2.4] (Site B). Controlled interrupted time-series analysis showed a significant immediate differential level change in median weekly hours to first action at Site A (-92.5%, 95% CI: -97.5% to -78.0%), and a significant downward trend at Site B (-43.5%, 95% CI: -65.2% to -8.2%). Changes in time to closure were directionally favorable but not statistically significant at either site. There was low use of the generated draft replies, only 0.5% at Site A and 3% at Site B. DiscussionImplementation of AI-assisted message categorization and routing was associated with a substantially reduced initial action time for patient In-Basket messages in Epilepsy. The utilization of AI-generated draft-replies to messages was low. These findings support the feasibility and effectiveness of AI-augmented workflows to improve inbox management. TAKE HOME POINTSO_LIAI-augmented In-Basket tools for categorization and routing of messages may substantially accelerate initial action on patient portal messages by directing messages to the appropriate staff. C_LIO_LIThere was low utilization of AI generated draft-replies. C_LIO_LIAuto-categorization and routing alone was not associated with reducing time to closure of messages. C_LI

papers.title: Fibromyalgia, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, and Multiple Sclerosis are associated with lower translocator protein binding affinity genotypes
papers.abstract: IntroductionNeuroinflammation is a known pathophysiologic mechanism in multiple sclerosis and a proposed mechanism in fibromyalgia and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the translocator protein (TSPO) has been widely used to measure neuroinflammation, though second-generation ligands are highly sensitive to a single nucleotide polymorphism, rs6971, resulting in high, mixed, and low affinity binders. It is unknown whether this polymorphism is associated with neuroinflammatory disorders. Materials and MethodsEighty-six total participant genotypes for TSPO binding affinity were identified through Sanger sequencing (30 fibromyalgia, 21 ME/CFS, 11 multiple sclerosis, and 24 healthy controls). Associations between patient group and genotype were assessed with Fishers Exact test. Associations between genotype and symptom severity from self-report questionnaires were assessed with Kruskal-Wallis tests. ResultsIn the present study individuals with fibromyalgia, (ME/CFS), or multiple sclerosis were more likely to have a mixed- or low-affinity genotypes compared to healthy controls. Presence of the low or mixed genotypes were also associated with greater self-reported fatigue severity and depressive symptoms. DiscussionThese findings should be confirmed in larger samples but suggest functional consequences of rs6971 polymorphism that may be related to the pathophysiology of pain and fatigue illnesses.

papers.title: Quantifying statistical power gains from prognostic modeling in Huntington's Disease
papers.abstract: Background and ObjectivesHuntingtons disease is a rare neurodegenerative disease in which optimizing clinical trial design is essential. Although baseline characteristics are known to predict disease progression, the statistical efficiency gains achievable by formally integrating prognostic predictions into trial analyses have not been systematically quantified. We aimed to benchmark prognostic modeling approaches, quantify the trial efficiency gains from prognostic covariate adjustment, and deliver a ready-to-deploy framework for immediate implementation. MethodsWe developed a two-step modeling pipeline using longitudinal Enroll-HD natural history data (NCT01574053) to train nine machine learning algorithms to predict disease progression across five UHDRS endpoints. For this, we used 16 predictive baseline covariates representing stage of disease (baseline score levels), disease specific (CAP, CAG length), demographics and co-medication use that could be quantified in one clinical visit. For Total Function Capacity (TFC), frequently used as a primary endpoint in clinical trials, we also devised a minimal prognostic model based on 6 covariates. Model performance was tested using the placebo arm of the GENERATION-HD1 phase 3 trial (NCT03761849). ResultsModels were trained on 16,398 Enroll-HD participants and tested on 260 participants from the GENERATION-HD1 placebo arm. Models that take into account nonlinear relationships between the covariates showed no performance advantage over linear-based models on the test set. For TFC, a minimal six-covariate linear prognostic model performed on par with the full 16-feature model. Adjusting for the prognostic score increased the signal-to-noise ratio across different trial visits by 8-18%, raising statistical power from 80% to up to 90% at a fixed sample size, or, equivalently, reducing required sample size by 15-28% compared to unadjusted analyses (no covariate adjustment). Compared to routinely used covariate adjustments (including baseline score, age, CAG repeat length, and CAP score), adjusting for a prognostic score consistently delivered meaningful additional efficiency gains. DiscussionPrognostic covariate adjustment using a simple six-covariate linear score derived from a single baseline visit yields meaningful gains in statistical power for HD clinical trials, while remaining fully embedded within standard, regulator-accepted analysis frameworks. This approach offers a practical and immediately deployable tool to improve trial design.

papers.title: Association Between Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio and Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation in Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: BackgroundPeripheral inflammation has been implicated in the pathophysiology of Parkinsons disease (PD), but its relationship wth autonomic dysfunction remains unclear. ObjectivesTo explore the association between peripheral inflammation, assessed by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and autonomic function in patients with PD. MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 97 patients with PD who underwent 123I-metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) cardiac scintigraphy and differential blood cell counts. Associations of NLR with early and delayed heart-to-mediastinum (H/M) ratios, washout ratio, and the coefficient of variation of R-R intervals (CVRR) were assessed using Spearmans rank correlation and multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and disease duration. ResultsNo significant univariable correlations were observed between NLR and the autonomic measures. In multivariable analysis, higher NLR was associated with a lower early H/M ratio (B = -0.802, 95% CI -1.598 to -0.005, P = 0.049), whereas no significant associations were observed with the delayed H/M ratio, washout ratio, or CVRR. Sensitivity analyses showed a generally consistent direction of association, although the effect estimate was attenuated after exclusion of two influential observations and statistical significance was not consistently retained. ConclusionsHigher NLR was associated with lower early cardiac MIBG uptake after adjustment for age, sex, and disease duration in patients with PD. This exploratory finding raises the possibility of an association between systemic inflammation and sympathetic dysfunction in PD and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Plasma biomarkers and incident clinical stage progression in the specialized memory clinic: a longitudinal study
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTIONThe utility of blood based Alzheimers disease (AD) biomarkers in predicting clinical trajectories remains uncertain. METHODSWe assessed the diagnostic and prognostic performance of p-tau181, p-tau217, GFAP, and NfL in a large memory{square}clinic cohort (n=3,645) with comprehensive baseline clinical evaluation and annual follow{square}up for up to three decades. RESULTSP-tau217, p-tau181 and GFAP were associated with amyloid-beta (A{beta}) pathology, while all biomarkers were elevated in AD and all-cause dementia. P-tau217 significantly outperformed others in detecting A{beta} pathology and clinical AD but performed similarly to NfL and GFAP for all-cause dementia. Prognostically, p{square}tau217 demonstrated the strongest association with cognitive decline, followed by GFAP and NfL, and best predicted progression status at 5{square} and 10{square} year intervals. All biomarkers provided added prognostic value beyond demographic and genetic covariates. DISCUSSIONThese findings support plasma biomarkers for disease identification and risk stratification while underscoring the need for population{square}specific approaches.

papers.title: Feature harmonization reveals that apparent cross-cohort differences in tau-positivity prediction reflect variable availability and cohort stage structure
papers.abstract: BackgroundCross-cohort machine-learning studies of tau positivity are increasingly used to assess generalizability of Alzheimers disease biomarker models, but apparent differences between cohorts may reflect clinical severity structure and cohort stage composition rather than genuine biological divergence. MethodsWe evaluated this problem across subject-level cohorts from the Alzheimers Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS3), and the National Alzheimers Coordinating Center (NACC) using harmonized tabular predictors and a feature-block ablation framework. For ADNI and OASIS3, we performed matched-feature analyses restricted to shared harmonized variables (age, APOE{varepsilon} 4, education, sex, the CDR(R) Dementia Staging Instrument sum-of-boxes score (CDR-SB), and the Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ)). Models were trained with five-fold stratified cross-validation using balanced logistic regression as the primary classifier. Random forests and extra-trees classifiers were evaluated as robustness checks and are reported in supplementary analyses. ResultsIn the primary matched-feature comparison, reference areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.851 for ADNI tau90, 0.860 for ADNI tau180, and 0.933 for OASIS3 tau180. Severity-only models retained 86-99% of reference performance, whereas demographic/genetic-only models retained 85-87%; bootstrap confidence intervals showed that the reference-minus-demo contrast remained positive across all primary cohorts. Before feature matching, OASIS3 showed substantially weaker demographic-only prediction (AUC{approx} 0.54), attributable to missing APOE and age variables. After harmonization with a matched feature set including age, the pre-harmonization demographic gap was no longer attributable to feature availability; the residual difference was most consistent with cohort disease-stage composition asymmetry, with CDR-SB = 0 prevalence of 84.5-88.7% in OASIS3 versus 49.3-51.7% in ADNI. ConclusionsThe original large ADNI-OASIS3 performance gap was largely a feature-availability artifact; after strict harmonization including age-field repair, the absolute gap narrowed and the signed ADNI-minus-OASIS3 difference reversed, with the residual difference most consistent with cohort disease-stage composition asymmetry. Clinical severity remains an important predictor across all cohorts, but the unique contributions of severity and demographic/genetic information depend strongly on stage composition. Cross-cohort biomarker modeling should account for both feature-set completeness and disease-stage composition heterogeneity, not only headline performance metrics.

papers.title: Biological age measured by DNA methylation clocks and neurodegenerative diseases: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Hallmarks of biological ageing are closely interconnected with neurodegenerative diseases. Deoxyribonucleic acid methylation (DNAm) clocks quantify biological age and may serve as peripheral biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to examine associations between DNAm-based biological age metrics and neurodegenerative diseases. Six databases were systematically searched from 1st January 2011 to 15th April 2026 for studies reporting associations between DNAm-based ages and neurodegenerative diseases including all-cause dementia, Parkinsons Disease, Multiple Sclerosis, and Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis. Correlated-and-hierarchical-effects meta-analyses were fitted using restricted maximum likelihood with Knapp-Hartung adjustment. Of 42,023 records screened, 37 observational studies (n=46 365; 60.5% female; median of mean age 69.4 years [IQR 62.5-73.3)) and seven Mendelian randomization studies met inclusion criteria. In longitudinal meta-analyses, higher GrimAge epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was significantly associated with higher dementia risk (HR per SD 1.11 [95% CI 1.02-1.20]; I{superscript 2} = 0.0%; p = 0.018), whereas Horvath1 EAA, Hannum EAA, PhenoAge EAA, and DunedinPACE were not significantly associated with dementia risk. Evidence for other neurodegenerative diseases were heterogeneous across clock generations and study designs. Mendelian randomization provided limited evidence for causality. Higher GrimAge EAA was the only DNAm age measure consistently predictive of higher all-cause dementia risk. Overall, however, DNAm age clocks show limited and inconsistent associations with neurodegenerative diseases, providing insufficient support for their use as disease biomarkers. These findings highlight the need to develop and independently validate disease-specific DNAm clocks and undertake pathway analyses to identify methylation changes associated with neurodegeneration and the biological processes they reflect.
